newsitem.title: UK: Copper sent back under $2,400, still ends higher.
newsitem.headline: Copper sent back under $2,400, still ends higher.

text.p: Copper prices were sent back under the $2,400 a tonne level during late Thursday LME ring and kerb trading, although the market still concluded the session higher.
Traders said the market's gains today were little more than a technical reaction to oversold momentum indicators after the sell-offs seen earlier this week.
Prices were unable to clear resistance around $2,415, and the subsequent slippage under $2,400 suggests that the seven-weeks lows of $2,355 hit yesterday are likely to come under attack again.

Market sentiment is likely to be influenced by rising stocks, with a 1,625-tonne increase today in LME warehouse inventories -- the fourth successive daily rise -- taking the running total this week to 3,200 tonnes.
Given the stock increases, which show signs of becoming the norm, and the summer slowdown, the market might now be tilting into surplus and so has little more scope on the upside.
Last trade was at $2,398 a tonne, well down from the high, but still $25 up from Wednesday's kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation remained at a solid $125, with July/August tight at $85/90.
Aluminium was steadier, but was unwilling to tackle the resistance between $1,580 and $1,600. However, falling stocks and forward consumer interest should restrict dips, as they did on Wednesday.
Last business was at $1,577 a tonne, up $8 from the previous kerb.
Zinc notched up a fresh near-seven year high during the afternoon, building on the strong raly from sub-$1,400 levels seen on Wednesday.
Many of the weaker longs have been shaken out, and further price advances are likely towards targets around $1,435. Last business was at $1,412, up $16.
Nickel prices remained above the support band pegged around $7,000/7,030, although market movements were inhibited by the lack of news from the Inco talks at Sudbury.
Talks resumed on Wednesday, but there have been no developments reported. Last trade was at $7,070, up $20 from Wednesday.
Lead trading was dull throughout, although the market ticked higher in the afternoon to end at $621, up $3 from yesterday.
Tin was unable to hold above $5,600, and tailed lower to close at $5,550, down $15. Alloy was quiet, and ended indicated at a little-changed $1,460/70.
